name: Reverse Pec Deck
grip: Neutral or pronated grip holding the horizontal or vertical machine handles at shoulder height.
description: Sit facing the chest support pad of a dual-function pec deck machine and horizontally abduct both arms outward and backward, isolating the posterior deltoids and external rotators.
setup: Adjust the seat height so the handles align directly with shoulder height when seated.
Set the machine arm stops to the rear-most position so handles meet directly in front of the chest.
Sit facing inward with chest pressed firmly against the vertical support pad and feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with straight wrists and a slight, fixed bend in both elbows.
instructions: Pull the handles outward and backward in a wide horizontal arc by contracting your rear deltoids.
Maintain the fixed, subtle elbow bend throughout the entire motion.
Continue until your arms are in line with your shoulders or slightly past, squeezing the back of your shoulders.
Slowly reverse the movement under control, resisting the weight stack until hands return to the front starting position.
cues: Keep chest pressed against the pad.
commonMistakes: Bending and straightening the elbows into a row instead of a fly.
Arching the spine and lifting the chest off the support pad to swing the load.
Shrugging the upper traps and pulling handles toward the neck.

logging.example: Stack pin set to 30 kg: record 30 kg selected machine load.
logging.note: Pec deck lever geometry and cam ratios vary between manufacturers; record selected stack pin load.

variantNote: Chest-supported reverse machine fly on a dual-function pec deck / rear delt machine, isolating posterior deltoids through guided horizontal abduction.
reviewNotes: Drafted from FitTrack ID 56 (Reverse Pec Deck).
Distinguished from anterior chest pec deck by inward-facing chest-supported orientation and horizontal abduction arc.
